claims.text: An enhanced free-energy integration method within DFT can predict the melting temperature of high-melting refractory materials.
The method can predict the entropy of fusion of high-melting refractory materials.
The method can predict the enthalpy of fusion of high-melting refractory materials.
The method can predict the volume change at the melting point of high-melting refractory materials.
Enhanced free-energy sampling greatly reduces computational expense relative to full AIMD thermodynamic integration.
Umbrella sampling or metadynamics can replace full ab initio thermodynamic integration in the proposed DFT workflow.
Enhanced sampling accelerates crossing of free-energy barriers associated with melting.
Crystalline-order or local-coordination parameters can differentiate the solid and liquid phases.
Enhanced sampling efficiently samples rare events associated with the solid-to-liquid phase transition.
More efficient exploration of the free-energy landscape enables extraction of melting properties with reduced simulation time.
The calculated melting properties will be in close agreement with results from full AIMD thermodynamic integration.
The enhanced method will obtain the melting-property results at significantly lower computational cost than full AIMD thermodynamic integration.
Accuracy may be compromised when the selected order parameters omit critical degrees of freedom.
Accuracy may be compromised when the enhanced-sampling calculation is not fully converged.
Complex melting behavior or extreme conditions may reduce the method's accuracy.
A discrepancy greater than 10% relative to full AIMD or established experimental data is proposed as the falsification threshold.
